prompt.en: A test transmitter on 6.3 MHz produces an unwanted signal at 18.9 MHz. Which explanation best fits the relationship?

text.en: It is the second harmonic because 18.9 is twice 6.3.
It is receiver desensitization because all multiples are receiver faults.
It is the third harmonic because 6.3 x 3 = 18.9.
It is a notch-filter effect because the unwanted signal is narrow.

explanation.en: A harmonic is an integer multiple of the fundamental; 18.9 divided by 6.3 equals 3.

prompt.en: You want to receive both below and above a strong utility transmitter near the middle of the range. Which filter family best matches that goal?

text.en: High-pass, because it removes both sides of the utility signal.
Band-reject, because it can attenuate the problem range while passing frequencies on both sides.
Low-pass, because it passes only the high side of the range.
Audio bypass, because RF filters work only in transmitters.

explanation.en: A band-reject filter removes a chosen range while leaving lower and higher frequencies available.

prompt.en: An SSB signal becomes wider and less intelligible after the microphone gain is raised. What is the best first correction?

text.en: Add a receiver notch filter at the other station.
Replace the feedline with a longer cable to lower the audio level.
Increase drive until the power meter stops moving.
Reduce the audio drive so the transmitter stays in its linear range.

explanation.en: Excessive audio drive can cause flat topping and splatter; backing off drive treats the source of the unwanted side energy.
